messages:
chloe: Customer reports duplicate POSTs when our TS SDK retries after an AbortController timeout. Happens on Node 18 + undici 5.9. Tried repro on local with 3s timeout and server that responds in 5s.

chloe: Minimal repro sent:```ts
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 3000);
await fetch('https://example.com/api/submit', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: JSON.stringify({x:1}),
  headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  signal: ac.signal,
  retry: { retries: 2, factor: 2, minTimeout: 100 } // SDK-level retry wrapper
});
```

chloe: Observed behavior: server logs show 2 POSTs, client shows one abort error then a retry that succeeds. Billing shows two charges (idempotency not applied).

tony: Are they using our SDK wrapper or raw fetch + our retry util?

chloe: Using our ts-sdk 1.14.0 wrapper that internally calls undici.fetch. The wrapper does a reattempt when it sees network errors.

victor: Common cause: AbortController abort triggers an error that our retry logic treats as retryable, but the original request may have still been transmitted by network stack (race). undici's documentation notes body streaming states can't be rewound by default.

chloe: Repro logs from client:```
Error: The operation was aborted
 at fetch (node:internal/deps/undici...)
 at sdkRetryWrapper (/src/sdk/retries.ts:48)
 retry attempt 1
 fetch succeeded on retry
```

chloe: Server logs:```
[12:01:02] POST /api/submit 200 id=abc123 payload={"x":1}
[12:01:05] POST /api/submit 200 id=def456 payload={"x":1}
```

tony: Do they set Idempotency-Key? If not, duplicate charges are expected when the first request actually landed.

chloe: No idempotency header was set. Customer expected SDK to avoid duplicate posts when AbortController used.

victor: Short-term recommendations:
- Advise using an Idempotency-Key on mutating endpoints.
- For fetch retries with non-rewindable bodies, clone/serialize the body ahead of time.
- Consider lowering Abort timeout or use a cancellation policy that waits for in-flight confirmation.

chloe: I drafted a reply with repro steps and mitigation, want eng signoff before I send.

eng-oncall: Quick check: which undici? 5.9? There were some signal ordering fixes in 5.10+. Also Node 20's fetch has differences.

chloe: Customer is on undici 5.9.0, node 18.15.

eng-oncall: OK. Two action items:
1) Recommend upgrade to undici >=5.10 to pick up signal handling fixes.
2) Add explicit idempotency guidance in our SDK docs and return a helper util `safeRetryPost` that clones JSON bodies and attaches `Idempotency-Key`.

tony: I'll open a tiny PR to docs and a small helper in the SDK. Also add a diagnostic flag to log when retry happens due to AbortError so support can correlate.

chloe: Customer-facing message: suggested steps and a repro they can run to confirm. I'll include server-side logs snippet and recommend idempotency and upgrade path.

victor: For engineering follow-up: investigate whether our retry wrapper should treat AbortErrors from AbortController as non-idempotent unless explicitly flagged. There is nuance: abort could be user cancellation vs network glitch.

support-bot: Note created: S-6421 - "ts-sdk abort-triggered retry causing duplicate POSTs" assigned to eng-oncall.

chloe: Thanks. I'll hold off on escalation until Tony's doc PR is up and we confirm the undici recommendation. :+1:

eng-oncall: If you can get us exact SDK callsite stack trace and customer's undici install, that will speed root cause. Also ask if they can try the same repro with `Idempotency-Key: test-123` to see if server de-dupes.

chloe: Will do. Sending reply now with those steps and logging request ids.

tony: PR opened: docs/guide/retries-idempotency.md and sdk/helpers/safeRetryPost.ts - will link once CI passes.

chloe: Closing loop with customer after they confirm.
